bearings.paper_claim: Relationships carry three attributes: content, direction and strength. A pair is tied by all the relationships it maintains. Strength can be carried as the value of a link, or considered within a presence-absence dichotomy by requiring a minimum frequency. Reported directed ties can be asymmetric, with the two sides reporting different amounts. The article does not say that thresholding discards strength.
bearings.paper_location: Relationships and Ties, printed pp. 326-328 (PDF pp. 4-6); asymmetric reporting at printed p. 327
bearings.system_side: Stage 3 builds sponsor-to-cosponsor edges summed per (From,To). Weight = role (1.0 original, 0.5 regular) times f_bill, where f_bill = success multiplier (3.0 if the bill passed its origin chamber, else 1) x bill decay weight x size norm (1/sqrt C under the default dial). moneyball_core NETWORKS cu config sets symmetrize True, so the cu cascade loader mean-symmetrizes each pair; holistic_norm keeps direction. The AUG workbook re-keys edges as (min,max); load_network_directed reads the BASE vintage.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The article gives design principles and no estimate. It does not address 2:1 role weights, the success multiplier, the decay factor or the sqrt size norm, and it does not show that symmetrizing changes diffusion. It is not evidence for keeping or dropping regular-cosponsor edges, so the rejected drop must not be defended from this paper. Asymmetric reports are a survey feature, not a graph-construction rule.
bearings.verifier_note: Analyst omitted the success and decay factors from f_bill. Analyst wrongly said the article holds that thresholding discards strength; the article says a threshold can still reflect strength in a dichotomy and does not say it discards it. The inference that the paper is consistent with keeping regular-cosponsor edges is not in the text. Code path verified.

bearings.paper_claim: Citing Coleman, Katz and Menzel (1966): some sources inform (mass media, drug salesmen) while others legitimate adoption; the legitimating sources, other doctors, were most influential, and close reciprocated ties carried legitimacy. Citing Granovetter (1973): over 80 percent of job information came from occasional or rare contacts, under 17 percent from frequent contacts.
bearings.paper_location: Printed p. 328 (Granovetter) and p. 337 (Coleman et al.) (PDF pp. 6, 15)
bearings.system_side: cpf_diffusion is 1.0 within party and 0.4+0.6*sqrt(bpf_u*bpf_v) across party. cpf_pressure is 1.7 co-partisan and 0.5 across party. Both feed p = x/(x+6) on the adjacency passed in.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Conceptual parallel only. The cited evidence concerns physicians and job seekers, not legislators, and the article gives no Coleman sample size or data-collection dates. It supports separating an information channel from a legitimation channel. It does not support the 1.7 and 0.5 ratios, the 0.4 floor or the constant 6. Coleman's reciprocated ties must not be imported as a reciprocity weight, since reciprocity is not validated (D-104 to D-108).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper quotes and both figures verified at printed pp. 328 and 337. Code factor values and the p formula verified in moneyball_core.py. Transfer caveats are sound.

bearings.paper_claim: Prominence is measured by degree (lines per actor) and by closeness (lowest sum of shortest-path distances). Brokerage is measured by betweenness. In Figure 3, after three arms are removed, actors B and C each keep degree 4 and actor A drops to degree 2, yet A still sits between the peripheral groups and keeps an intermediary role.
bearings.paper_location: Prominence, printed pp. 334-335; Brokerage, printed pp. 335-336 (PDF pp. 12-14), Figure 3
bearings.system_side: InfluenceScore = 0.60 weighted out-degree + 0.25 betweenness + 0.15 eigenvector, renormalized over components present, each min-max scaled. Computed with igraph on the directed weighted graph with path distance 1/W.
bearings.transfer_conditions: A taxonomy of measures, with no evidence on which predicts legislative influence. It does not bear on the stance-sign retirement. Whether centrality predicts passage belongs to Sotoudeh 2024 and the system data.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and Figure 3 logic verified. Weights and igraph calls verified in the R code. Not verified: the 2026-06-25 retirement date and AB13 flag, which lie outside the text and code ranges checked.

bearings.paper_claim: Brokerage is a positional property separate from prominence. Actors on a path between networks, or spanning a structural hole between unconnected clusters, control flow between them, and betweenness measures this. A path that spans a structural hole is particularly useful.
bearings.paper_location: Brokerage, printed pp. 335-336; position and paths, printed p. 338 (PDF pp. 13-14, 16)
bearings.system_side: Staffer graph publishes PageRank at damping 0.85 (sensitivity at 0.70 and 0.95) and a component-local eigenvector. Bridging score is normalized Simpson diversity of row-normalized tie mass across target kinds. No betweenness or Burt-constraint score found in fec/staffer_network.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Any span score added must describe graph structure only, not access or introduction probability (D-025). Staffer edges are co-tenure and revolving-door ties, so the paper's control-of-flow wording must not carry over. Payroll container cliques are built in by construction. The r = 0.87 degree versus office size figure was not checked.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claims and code descriptions verified. Bridging measure is composition across node kinds, so the suggested span measure is not already present.

bearings.paper_claim: Relationship strength is its intensity, for example how many goods are exchanged or how often actors meet, and it can be kept as a value rather than dichotomized. At the tie level, measures combine frequency of contact, duration, intimacy, reciprocal services and kinship, and they depend on context.
bearings.paper_location: Strength and Tie Strength, printed pp. 327-328 (PDF p. 5)
bearings.system_side: Co-tenure weight = kappa x tier x (1 - exp(-days/tau)) x attenuation, with tau = 365.2425. Shared-role factor 0.05 attenuates shared titles.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Principle only: strength should be valued and duration is one input. The article gives no functional form, time constant or proximity multiplier, so tau and the kappa ladder remain owner design. The kappa ladder values were not located in ranking_math.py and are unverified here. The weight is a heuristic exposure score, not a contact probability (D-025).
bearings.verifier_note: Formula and constants verified in code. Analyst paraphrase merged relationship-level intensity with the tie-level list of combined measures; corrected here. Kappa ladder values not verified.

bearings.paper_claim: Structure is derived from observed relationships, not from a priori classes. The article lists membership in organizations among the a priori classifications it avoids as a basis for groups. Cliques form among similar people and limit nonredundant information. Density is actual over possible links, with n(n-1) possible directed ties (380 for n = 20).
bearings.system_side: Person-person edge requires concurrent service in the same container, weighted by guaranteed overlap times kappa. Admin containers are excluded. Rule of record is the brain note concepts/concurrent-service-overlap-edge-rule.md, which exists. The 1.00 to 0.40 kappa ladder and the 70.8 percent figure were not located and are unverified.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The article would treat container co-presence as a membership-based classification, close to the a priori organizational class it warns against, not as an observed exchange. Density and clique statistics inside a container are produced by construction. The article gives no link between co-presence and actual exchange. No edge may be described in influence or access terms.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper count and principle verified. Analyst transfer called container co-presence shared class membership giving an opportunity for exchange, which understates the article's warning against membership-based classes. Corrected. Admin exclusion verified in code.

bearings.paper_claim: Pairs are tied by all the relationships they maintain. The strength of a tie may depend on the number and types of relationships a pair maintains, and on the strength of each relationship.
bearings.system_side: On the CU base a media edge is admitted only for pairs with no cosponsor tie (untied). Holistic configs default to dominance: a tied pair takes max(cosponsor, media). HCoI edges are admitted only for cosponsor-isolated members, at weight up to 0.12. A second channel can raise a tied pair to the larger of the two weights, but the layers are never summed.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Multiplexity is conceptual and comes from survey-based ego networks. Here the layers are corpora of different quality. The untied and max rules are deliberate guards ruled by Paul, not recommendations to sum layers.
bearings.verifier_note: Analyst said a second channel never raises strength in either case. The code uses max under dominance, so a second channel can raise a tied weight to the larger value. Corrected above. Paper claim verified.

bearings.paper_claim: Block modelling finds structurally equivalent actors by correlating all pairs of cases and then clustering the correlations. Structural equivalence means identical ties to and from all other actors. Structure should come from observed relationships rather than attribute classes. The article does not name tie-matrix rows as the profile that is correlated.
bearings.paper_location: Structural equivalence, printed p. 334 (PDF p. 12); relational view, printed p. 325
bearings.system_side: press_hcoi.py correlates members' press-category attention profiles across 19 categories, keeps r >= 0.6, and runs Louvain with seed 7. The multilayer builder admits HCoI only for cosponsor-isolated members, at weight 0.6*r*HCOI_W capped at 0.12, as an explicit non-collaboration claim. The code docstring cites Malaterre and Lareau 2024 as the method source.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The procedure resembles block modelling but correlates attributes rather than relationships, so under the article's definitions HCoI is attribute similarity. That supports keeping it as a weak, surgical layer. The article says nothing on whether attention similarity predicts collaboration.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper does not say the correlated profiles are rows of the tie matrix; corrected. Code thresholds, seed, and weight cap verified. The homophily replication claim was not checked.

related.why: The article names degree and closeness (prominence) and betweenness (brokerage) without testing them; it does not name eigenvector. Sotoudeh tests cosponsorship centrality measures against bill passage.
The article surveys degree, closeness and betweenness. The Katz and PageRank choices attributed to Ardekani are not in this article, so the link is only the shared centrality family.

press_hcoi.py takes its method from Malaterre and Lareau (2024), which correlates text profiles. The article's relational view bears on attribute-based grouping, but it does not discuss text profiles, so no direct contradiction is shown.

The article's cohesion and clustering section (density, cliques, clusters, printed pp. 332-333) and its co-membership examples (printed p. 326) are the framework that committee co-membership analysis applies. Porter's content was not checked here.
The article cites Coleman, Katz and Menzel for the inform versus legitimate split (printed p. 337). Box-Steffensmeier offers congressional evidence on cue-taking. Its content was not checked here.

The article says close reciprocated ties carry legitimacy (Coleman et al., printed p. 337), the in-group legitimation mechanism that partisan cue work would test. Bakker's content was not checked here.
The article's content, direction and strength triad (printed pp. 326-328) has no sign dimension, which signed-network methods add.
The article's tie-strength and similarity-selection discussion (printed pp. 327-328, 336) is conceptual background for friendship tie-formation work. Selfhout's content was not checked here.

summary_issues: Year: the text header reads LISR 18, 323-342 (1998); the 1996 hint is the ALISE conference year. The ext correction to 1998 is right.
summary_md says cutting strength at a frequency threshold throws information away. The article does not say that; it says strength can still be considered within a presence-absence dichotomy.
summary_md says the article warns against threshold cutting. No such warning appears; the wording should be neutral.
summary_md says edges are scaled by 1/sqrt of the cosponsor count. f_bill also includes the 3.0 success multiplier and the bill decay weight (congress_member_scraper.R:1927).

summary_md and gaps_exposed say the cascade kernel runs on an undirected graph. That holds for the cu config (symmetrize True); holistic_norm stays directed (moneyball_core.py:398-400). Scope the claim.
